Prepare to die, fool!
Little fool! I must do nothing, particular not at the command of a pitiful <man/woman> such as you!
<StartAction>[Ghasaran snickers at you.]</Start> Yes, it seems that I am...
Men! Secure the doors! Let us spill the blood of these fools for the glory of the Mother of Death!
<StartAction>[Suddenly, Ghasaran's men swing the doors to the chamber shut, quickly barring them and securing the lock. It appears you are trapped in here along with Kara...]</Start>

<StartAction>[The terrifying visage of the man called Ghasaran looks down upon you.]</Start> So, you have returned, <Race> <man/woman>, and I hope you have reconsidered telling us where we may find the witch we seek!
<StartAction>[Before you stands a man adorned in blood red armor, his face concealed behind a hideous mask. Just the mere sight of him is enough to send shivers running down your spine...]</Start>
<StartAction>[The fearsome man points at you.]</Start> You there! <Race> <man/woman>! I must speak with you!
<StartAction>[The man grabs you roughly by the arm.]</Start> You will hear me out, <Race> <man/woman>, for such is my demand, and none refuse me!
<StartAction>[You hear a deep snarl from within the depths of the man's helm.]</Start> You would be wise to listen to my words, <Race> <man/woman>, for you may be rewarded well for your aid!

<StartAction>[The man appears on the brink of lashing out at you, but after a long moment, he finally backs away.]</Start> Go then! Return to me should you desire the opportunity to be well rewarded with a purse of 500 gold pieces!
So, little worm, do you have any last words before joining this witch in death?!
I am Ghasaran, and I seek your aid! I have heard word that you witnessed the summoning of a spirit of the Underworld in this city, and I desire to know where I may find the witch who called it forth!
Tell me of her whereabouts, and you shall be rewarded well with a purse of 500 gold pieces!
<StartAction>[Ghasaran growls at you menacingly.]</Start> So be it, <Race> <man/woman>! We shall simply have to find the witch on our own! Do not worry... She will not escape our grasp for long!
<StartAction>[Ghasaran motions for his lackeys to accompany him, and they quickly depart...]</Start>

<StartAction>[Ghasaran looks down upon you, as though searching your mind for the truth of your answer.]</Start> So be it! We must go in search of the witch at once, before she has a chance to escape our clutches!
For now, I shall give you half of your promised reward... To claim the other half, I must insist you come to the witch's location, and ensure that we procure her with no difficulty...

<StartAction>[An unearthly growl rumbles inside Ghasaran's mask.]</Start> You shall demand nothing of me! Either accept my terms or refuse them, but I shall pay you no more until the witch is in our custody!
<StartAction>[You can feel Ghasaran's icy stare bearing down into you.]</Start> You will accept it, or receive no reward, fool! I must ensure that you are telling the truth, now mustn't I?
Come join us in abducting the witch, and when the deed is done, you shall be paid in full... <StartAction>[Apparently considering the matter resolved, Ghasaran turns away from you.]</Start>
<StartAction>[Ghasaran motions for his lackeys to accompany him, and they quickly depart in the direction you pointed them...]</Start>

That is a matter which does not concern you, little fool, and one which I am quite afraid you will not live long enough to learn... Now, prepare to meet the Mother of Death, and accept her cold embrace!
<StartAction>[Ghasaran looks down upon you, as though searching your mind for the truth of your answer.]</Start> So be it! We shall go at once to find the witch at this tavern!
For now, I shall give you half of your promised reward... To claim the other half, I must insist you come to the witch's location, and ensure that we procure her with no difficulty...

<StartAction>[An unearthly growl rumbles inside Ghasaran's mask.]</Start> You shall demand nothing of me! Either accept my terms or refuse them, but I shall pay you no more until the witch is in our custody!
<StartAction>[You can feel Ghasaran's icy stare bearing down into you.]</Start> You will accept it, or receive no reward, fool! I must ensure that you are telling the truth, now mustn't I?
Come join us in abducting the witch, and when the deed is done, you shall be paid in full... <StartAction>[Apparently considering the matter resolved, Ghasaran turns away from you.]</Start>
<StartAction>[Ghasaran motions for his lackeys to accompany him, and they quickly depart in the direction you pointed them...]</Start>
That is for us to know only! It is of no concern to you! If you wish to receive your reward, you will cooperate with us fully!
<StartAction>[Ghasaran shakes visibly in anger.]</Start> If you must know, the woman we seek is a traitor to our holiest of orders, and we seek to bring vengeance upon her!
<< Set owner's journal quest to "JT_PREL_KARA_2" >>

<StartAction>[Ghasaran cackles evilly.]</Start> True, but you are also no longer of use to me either... Do not worry, though. Your soul shall pass to the Mother of Death, and such a sacrifice will please her greatly...
<< This conversation node does nothing but reset the variable "N_TALK_SWITCH" >>
Now, prepare to die, fool!
<StartAction>[Ghasaran lowers his mace, and prepares to engage you in combat... His men jump eagerly into the fray...]</Start>
<StartAction>[Ghasaran nods approvingly in your direction.]</Start> So we have the daughter of Dy'nesh in our grasp! The Dark Mother will be pleased...
You have done well, <Race> <man/woman>, in leading us to the Elven witch... but I am afraid your usefulness has come to an end...
Oh, but I do believe it is you that are mistaken, little fool! Soon, you shall feel the fury of the Mother of Death unleashed upon you, and accept her dark embrace...
Why do you want Kara so badly?
What's this? You're going to betray me?!
Excuse me, but I do not have time for this nonsense right now...
Well there's a first time for everything! Now move out of my way!
I told you once to move out of my way... I shall not repeat it again!
Why do you wish me dead?
<StartAction>[Leave the presence of this strange man as quickly as you can.]</Start>
That's quite a reward... Perhaps we should talk this out a bit further...
I'm sorry, but do I know you?
Who are you? What do you want from me?
Give me some time to think about it, and perhaps I'll take you up on your offer...
I am sorry, but I must refuse your request. I simply do not trust the look of you...
<StartAction>[Lie.]</Start> I believe I saw the woman you seek heading towards the docks... You might be able to find her there...
I demand you give me all the payment at this moment!
That was never part of our agreement!
Very well. I shall meet you there...
<StartAction>[Truth.]</Start> The woman you seek, an Elven maiden by the name of Kara Dy'nesh, is staying at the Ravenclaw Tavern...
I demand you give me all the payment at this moment!
That was never part of our agreement!
Very well. I shall meet you there...
Why do you want to find this woman so badly?
No... First you tell me why you want her, then I'll decide whether to help you or not...
That's fair enough...
You won't take me without a fight! <StartAction>[Launch into an attack against Ghasaran and his men.]</Start>
You are making a foolish mistake if you think you can cross me!
I demand you pay me the remaining gold you promised, and allow me to leave in peace!

<StartAction>[The man standing before you gives a welcoming grin, but his eyes glint with a dangerous light.]</Start> So, you are here on business from Shrak, I take it? On behalf of the Bloodhawks, I welcome you.

<StartAction>[The Bloodhawk looks around the room, his eyes narrowing.]</Start> I assume if you have sought us out, you have someone in mind you'd like to be rid of. Yet I see you are alone. We Bloodhawks do not like to be toyed with...
Go retrieve this slave of yours, and bother us no more until then! <StartAction>[The Bloodhawk motions for you to leave the room, and refuses to speak to you further.]</Start>
<StartAction>[The Bloodhawk turns his gaze towards Markius, and his smile broadens.]</Start> I see you have brought your 'companion' with you... He seems to be a fine specimen indeed...
We shall lead you to our master. He'll be very pleased with the both of you... <StartAction>[The two Bloodhawks smile at you and you get the sense that something is horribly wrong.]</Start>

<StartAction>[Suddenly you feel a stinging in your neck. Raising your hand to it, you feel the feathered end of a small dart. Your vision already beginning to blur, you see Markius stagger and fall to the floor. The room whirls around you but you feel no impact....]</Start>

<StartAction>[You come upon Markius Albright and his companions, apparently having cornered the Crimson Prophet here within the Docks...]<StartAction>
Destroy these fools while I escape to my ship! Let the Sharakhan Empire cower in fear before the might of the Crimson Prophet!
<StartAction>[You find yourself unable to move as the Crimson Prophet draws near to you, his strange eyes locking with yours.]</Start> So, you have lowered the Control Stone's shields...

Quite clever of you, <lad/lass>... but it matters not! I have retrieved what I have come for... <StartAction>[The Prophet holds forth a black jewel, red flames dancing along its smooth surface...]</Start>

<StartAction>[Harkon slowly turns his head towards the Crimson Prophet, struggling against the sorceries holding him in place.]</Start> You shall not take that gem, Prophet! By Rakha's name, I swear it!
<StartAction>[The Crimson Prophet sneers.]</Start> Rakha holds no power over me, petty sorcerer! No, I believe there is little you can do to stop me...
And to ensure you bother me no further, I believe I shall leave you to my followers... <StartAction>[The Prophet motions for his followers to enter the chamber...]</Start>
Finish them, Followers of the Crimson Path! Show these fools what fate lies in store for those who stand in the way of the Crimson Prophet!
<StartAction>[As the Crimson Prophet departs, he waves his hand in a wide arc, causing the doors of the Control Stone chamber to slam shut and seal behind him...]</Start>
<< Set owner's journal quest to "JT_ST_1_MAIN" >>

Your days are finished, Prophet! You shall never leave Ghaarak with that jewel! <StartAction>[Harkon begins gesturing his hands in preparation for a spell...</Start>
<< This conversation node does nothing but reset the variable "N_TALK_SWITCH" >>
<StartAction>[As Harkon releases his sorceries upon the Crimson Prophet, a strange magical sphere arises around the red robed figure, stopping the spell before it can reach him...]</Start>
Did you truly think that I, the Crimson Prophet, would fall to such a pitiful display of power, fool?! No! I'm afraid it is you who shall fall this night!
<StartAction>[The Crimson Prophet utters a single word, unleashing a powerful magical blast which sends Harkon reeling to the ground...]</Start>
To me, ShadowGuard! The Crimson Prophet must not be allowed to escape!
<StartAction>[The Crimson Prophet looks upon his oncoming attackers in disinterest.]</Start> I grow tired of your meddling in my affairs, fools!
<StartAction>[You see the Crimson Prophet raise his hand in the air, calling forth a vile cloud which covers the docks and sends everyone nearby to the ground, reeling in nausea...]</Start>
Now, I believe I shall be on my way... but before I do, I shall leave you with some companions to keep you... preoccupied... while I make my escape...
By order of Imperial Officer Ganolin, under the Law of Rakha, we hereby place you, Nelgir, under arrest on the charge of murder...
Hello <FirstName>, what can I do for you?

Hi <FirstName>! Aren't you excited? It's our final day as lowly subjects of the Empire and our first as true citizens! Or at least it will be as soon as we can get through this ceremony. Is there anyway I can help with the Judgement?

You can take the druid out of the wood but you can't take the wood out of the druid, isn't that what they say? <StartAction>[Janthos gives Alia a friendly punch on the shoulder.]</Start> We'll miss you, Alia, but we won't keep you.
And I will miss both of you. You've both been the most wonderful friends a girl could dream of. Come on, <FirstName>. Stop stalling and let's be done with this Judgement.

Rakha protects the Empire. Even before there was an Empire, he protected the people of the cities and the trees of the forest. He's done so much for all of us who follow his teachings. With all he's done for the forest, I think he may be a brother druid.

A druid? That's a joke, right? Rakha has the heart of an inventor. He's designed the entire Empire to perfection: every citizen has a role, every city its defenses. He doesn't have time to worry about the trees, Alia. He has people like you to do that.
Oh, and you've met Emperor Rahka, have you? No, I didn't think so! Anyway, I was helping <FirstName>, so there...

Oh, I guess great <Lord/lLady> <FirstName>, the pompous noble, has the Emperor over for tea on a daily basis! <StartAction>[Alia offers a wicked grin that the seems to save especially for you.]</Start>
I'm sure the mighty and powerful High <Lord/Lady> <FullName>, <CUSTOM6001> of the great Magistrate, has the Emperor shining <his/her> shoes each morning on the way to class!
All right, all right. Enough of this jest. <StartAction>[Alia winks at you.]</Start> Do you have any other questions, your <lord/lady>ship?

I guess it doesn't, really. <StartAction>[Alia offers you a puzzled frown.]</Start> Whatever the Emperor is, he seems to hold the peace and protection of his citizens in high regard and we all have that to be thankful for at the very least.

A what!? <He/She>'s even crazier than you are, Janthos. <StartAction>[Alia shakes her head, a confused expression on her face.]</Start> In any case, Rakha is the one who brings us hope in dark times like these.

I can't imagine not having them! They traveled for three days from Lac Brier so they could be here, even with the floods. They're exhausted and haven't even unpacked the mules but they wouldn't have missed the ceremony for all the world.

Well whatever Rakha is, he protects the cities *and* the forests. He's a hero to be respected, and he saved us all from dread King Khagrim. He's a good leader in these times of peril and that's what matters.
That much we can agree upon! <StartAction>[Janthos grins widely, the original dispute already long forgotten.]</Start> Now what were you asking Alia again?

I don't know. I was staying with my family in the forest at the time and we really don't pay much attention to what happens here in the city... With the exception of the Academy, of course... I'm not sure what to tell you, <FirstName>.

You don't remember the "Black Butcher?" The heralds were calling out the news throughout half the Empire two years ago! Foolish druids. If a bird falls sick in the forest, you all know of it but if a hundred city-folk are killed you never hear a thing!

Two years? His spirit has been trapped here for that long? It's not natural! He should have been sent to the afterlife! It's up to the Spirit Cycle to cleanse sins from the dead, no matter what their crime.

Please, <FirstName>, the spirit of any living thing should be allowed to pass on when it dies. The Spirit Cycle spirit is a natural thing, as plain as breathing. We have no right to interfere in it, not even as citizens of the Empire.
Blah blah blah. Yakir is a heinous criminal, an abomination to your precious nature, not a part of it. If Rahka holds him to this plane, it's for good reason!

<He/She> asked me about the Spirit Cycle, Janthos, so kindly keep your comments to yourself. You see, <FirstName>, we all pass through the cycle of life, death, and rebirth. It's a natural process and helps maintain balance in the world.

People are born. In life, they make their choices, sowing the seeds of imbalance in the world. In death, the balance is restored through the blessings and punishments of Heaven and Hell so they can be reborn, pure and new, into the world.
To trap him here, away from Heaven or Hell, is to preserve that imbalance. If he is as evil as Janthos claims, then you have made the world more evil by keeping him here. Don't you see, Janthos?
You're a lucky girl, Alia. Your parents really love you, especially your mother! She seems nearly ecstatic about you gaining citizenship.

Hogwash! He made his bed and he should lie in it, Alia. If he really is going to be reborn like you claim, he'll just make the same choices all over again and how many other people will lose their families over it? Don't let it happen, <FirstName>... I beg you...
W-What did you call me!? You arrogant, highborn scum! Nobles like you know nothing of the people's suffering! You're nothing but the spoiled seed of your greater father!
<StartAction>[Alia stares slack-jawed at the both of you.]</Start> Please, stop this bickering! Janthos, I'd have thought your rage would be spent by now!

And <FirstName>, your rudeness falls far below your rank! If you're going to be a dignitary like your father, you should try to be a little more diplomatic. I wouldn't have believed you capable of tormenting poor Janthos like that.

<StartAction>[Alia's face brightens with rage.]</Start> Why you filthy weasel! Actually, even a weasel has more honor than the likes of you! Well I won't let a tomfool noble<man/woman> like you ruin the day I gain my citizenship...
No wonder the Magistrate never came. Even your own father is too embarrassed to claim you as his own! Why, you should be-- <StartAction>[Janthos places a concerned hand on Alia's shoulder.]</Start>
Uh... I didn't mean for it to come to this, <FirstName>. This is our citizenship day and, well... we're all friends, right? Make what Judgement you must and let's move on, okay?
Yes, I... I let my temper get away with me. You are right about that much, Janthos. Now if the young <Lord/Lady> <LastName> has any more questions of me, <he/she> may ask...
Then perhaps you should develop some! Both of you are in the wrong here. I doubt you'll apologize to me or anyone but I will not let you ruin the day of my citizenship.

<StartAction>[Janthos grows pale as Alia turns her back on the both of you.]</Start> Wait! I apologize! I do... My outburst was uncalled for, and my rage... misdirected. I take responsibility for my actions.
Mom was pregnant with me when graduated from this Academy and wasn't able to attend the final ceremony so in some ways this one is for the both of us.
Well... Thank you, Janthos. I would not have excepted a gnome to be the bigger person in this argument... Come, we have a Judgement to perform, <FirstName>. Do you have any more questions for me?
I apologize, too. It's not you I was angry at, <FirstName>, but allow me to take responsibility for my actions all the same. They were inappropriate.
It's all right. I take responsibility for my rant and the argument that followed. My outburst was uncalled for too, <FirstName>.
Now isn't it better when things fall back into balance? Now, back to the task at hand: Is there anything more I can help you with, <FirstName>?

<StartAction>[Janthos glares at you briefly but his gaze soon softens.]</Start> You know I lost my parents to brigands. I didn't mean to lash out like that but you must learn to be more sensitive to other people's feelings, mine included.
But I do ask that you let Rakha hold Yakir here where he can do no more damage. For the families still mourning their losses, if nothing else.
Well, let's agree to disagree, then. We've both come to our decisions honestly and you with more loss than I.
Oh, I'm so sorry, Janthos! This must remind you terribly of your loss. I can get so caught up in things and I... I wasn't thinking.
No, it's my fault. I can't mourn forever, can I? It's not you that I'm mad at. It never is... Please, excuse me.
Oh I'm sorry, Janthos. I know the memories this must be dredging up for you. I thought you had finally put your anger over what happened to your parents to rest.

It's good to see them again, though. It's been so long since I last went home. <StartAction>[Alia glances at her mother's smiling, tear-stained face and gives a little wave.]</Start> Your father will arrive soon, <FirstName>. I know he will...

I apologize. Please forgive my outburst, both of you. I have strong opinions on this matter but it's not my place to force them onto either of you, especially when you've been such good friends to me. Please, let's get on with the Judgement.
It's so clear but on the other hand it's so complicated. I mean, Emperor Rakha has my trust and respect and I know he only does what is right... but then why would he even allow us a choice?
If I'm to Judge by my conscience, then I think his spirit should be set free and allowed to travel to Heaven or Hell in accordance with the natural Spirit Cycle.
Are you okay? I didn't realize you felt so strongly about the Judgement... Thank you for freeing the spirit, at least. I just wish you were doing it for different reasons, that's all.
There are many means to an end but some paths in life are more dangerous than others. Be objective, that's all I ask...

Thank you, <FirstName>. Yakir's spirit won't go unpunished for his crimes in this life and the spirit cycle will cleanse him and give him another chance in the next. I know how hard a decision it was to make.

W-Wow! I've never heard such an eloquent statement, <FirstName>! Like it or not, your father's highborn blood runs thick in your veins... It's a good thing, <Lord/Lady> <LastName> and something to be proud of!
It looks like you've made your decision, <FirstName>. You really should have released the spirit to the underworld, but I believe your intentions were good.

That may be true. Oh, don't look at me like that! I know I am an idealist and I know that I've never lost anyone close to me, not like you and Janthos... But, even so, you should'nt judge others unless you're able to be objective about it.

Time at the Academy moves quickly for you, doesn't it... As for me, I love you all dearly but I can't help to get back to the woods. The druid council said they'd name me as a true druid on my return.
A true druid and a true citizen of the Empire! Won't it be wonderful, <FirstName>?
Okay, what would you like to know?

Home is home and family is family. My parents will stay here long enough to recover from the journey then we'll leave for the woods. I don't know if I'll ever even come back to the city... It's a long journey, <FirstName>...
Excuse me.
Glad to have your parents here?
What do you think of Emperor Rakha?
All you filthy peasants claiming Rakha as your own...
Why does it matter what Rakha is?
What if Rakha's a druidic engineer?
I'm pretty sure Rakha's a <class>, like me.
What do you know of Yakir?
What do you mean by "Spirit Cycle"?
Enough whining, fool.
I will not apologize for my actions, peasant.
Hmpf! Diplomacy is a skill I will not learn.
Sorry about that, Janthos.
I apologize, my behavior was uncalled for.
Have we struck a nerve, Janthos?
What are you talking about?
Are you all right, Janthos?
I wish I'd had more time to get to know you.
What Judgement would you cast, Alia?
I refuse to accept your foolish notions.
Natural law before mortal law, Alia...
You've never lost someone close to you, Alia.
Let's talk about something else.
Why can't you stay here in the city?
Still pondering what to do about Yakir, are you, <FirstName>?
Greetings and congratulations, <FirstName>! Today we become full citizens. It's really quite exciting, don't you think? I know a little about this Yakir fellow, if you're interested.
It's always about my golems, isn't it Alia? <StartAction>[Sigh.]</Start> Where is your father, <FirstName>? I'd have expected he'd be here today.
Hey! No need for hostilities, <FirstName>. I'm sure he'll be along before the closing of the ceremony.
I trust he will make it. He cares for you greatly but bears a substantial burden as the community's Magistrate. You should try to understand his position as well as your own.
The title of Magistrate is a heavy burden on even the strongest men. However, I seriously doubt your father would miss this. Keep your eyes open; I'm sure he'll be here shortly.
I'm sure he will. I'm surprised he's not here already, to be honest. I can't count the number of time he's stopped by the Academy to discuss your progress with the instructors.
I'm sure Janthos is right. Your father's offices are near enough; I'm sure he'll be here before the ceremony ends.
Is there anything else you'd like to know?

<StartAction>[The gnome chuckles wryly.]</Start> I know you're trying to buy time until your father arrives but this is hardly the time or the place to be swapping well-worn stories with each other. After the ceremony, maybe. I'll be out in the courtyard.
Working on your mechanical monstrosities, I have no doubt. Must your projects always be so unnatural and dangerous, Janthos?
Druids... This feat of engineering is a true testament to my... uh... Actually, what was I saying about well-worn stories? I'll show you what I mean out in the courtyard later, okay <FirstName>?

My folks? Well... I don't remember much. They passed on when I was very young. I was only eight or so when the Academy took me in. I know my acceptance was an act of pity but it gave me more hope than I would have found on the streets.

Some called him the "Black Butcher" but others call him much worse. He was a small-time sorcerer until two years ago. One afternoon he started hurling fireballs and summoning demons in the city streets.
In his short but bloody rampage he killed over a hundred and twenty people. Most were women and children. After the guard sealed his power, he was tried and summarily executed for his crimes.

A truly awful sort. I'm glad to see he's still being held under Rakha's power and, if you ask me, that's where he should stay! Rakha will make him pay for his crimes more thoroughly than hell ever could.
Well that seems a little harsh!

Murder is a pretty harsh thing, Alia. Especially a hundred murders! I have no pity for those who kill for sport... But enough talk of dark deeds. It makes my skin crawl. Is there anything else you'd like to know, <FirstName>?

You know how I feel about this, <FirstName>. Yakir's a rebel and a criminal of the most despicable sort. He should be caged and confined, with every right and freedom stripped from him forever. I say we leave him in Rakha's keeping.
What was that all about!? You let the spirit go and insulted the academy! Why do you insist on being so arrogant, <FirstName>?
You should not insult one who has given us so much. It is not my place to berate you for your foolishness but, rest assured, your father will hear of this.
Well, it seems you've made your decision. The spirit is free. I don't agree with your Judgement but Yakir's fate was yours to decide, not mine.
I... I understand your point. He will surely suffer an eternity for what he has done. I still feel that he deserves worse than what Hell has to offer, though...

My parents died during a winter blizzard. A band of brigands had come upon our home in the forest and my father's conscience wouldn't let them freeze in the snow. He unbarred the door and invited them in.
So that was the Judgement. I'd like to thank you, <FirstName>. I'm sure that more good will come by leaving the spirit in Rakha's care than by setting it free.
I agree wholeheartedly. The victims of Yakir's vile actions can rest easy tonight. Thanks again, <FirstName>.
My father was a warm-hearted man. He gave the three travelers food and a warm spot by the fire to wait out the winter storm. In less then a hour they had revealed their true nature.
